newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada dlr opens stronger amid buying against mark.
newsitem.headline: Canada dlr opens stronger amid buying against mark.

text.p: * The Canadian dollar opened stronger on Wednesday at C$1.3757 (US$O.7269) amid some buying against the German mark and purchases by Canadian banks. * Dealers said Greenspan's comments reduced U.S. rate hike fears and took pressure off the Canadian currency. * Outlook for session seen positive if currency can breach C$1.3750 (US$0.7273) level.

Speculation that Greenspan might deliver a hawkish message to the House Banking subcommittee of the U.S. Congress as part of his semi-annual Humphrey-Hawkins testimony weighed on the Canadian dollar earlier on Tuesday.
However, in his testimony Greenspan suggested there was no need to raise U.S. interest rates now because U.S. economic growth was slowing.
The comments sparked a rally in North American financial markets, with the Canadian dollar, bonds and equity markets all strengthening.

A U.S. rate hike would be negative for the Canadian dollar because it would lure capital flows away from Canada. A U.S. rate hike would also put pressure on the Bank of Canada to raise interest rates here.
Analysts said that given Greenspan's comments, the Canadian dollar now has the potential to appreciate further.

"We're looking for a range of C$1.3735-85. A break of C$1.3750 would be significant and probably allow us to trade down to that C$1.3735 level," said Farrill. "If we get a clean break there (at C$1.3750) then Canada should be off to the races."
On the crosses, the Canadian dollar rose against the German mark to 1.3287 marks from 1.3222 marks at Tuesday's close. The unit rose to 83.62 yen from 83.45 yen.
